subject: Post-call: segmentation commitment & deployment expectations
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwell-analytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 09:12 PDT
Subject: Post-call: segmentation commitment & deployment expectations

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so nothing gets lost: 

Summary of what we heard
- Clearwell needs a deployment where customer data (PHI-derived telemetry) is logically separated from other customers. Primary concern: isolation of model input/output and access to system logs.
- Preferred residency: US-only.
- Security controls requested: customer-managed key (BYOK), strict audit logs, and a way to demonstrate no control-plane access for data plane tokens.

Options we discussed (high-level)
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding but does not meet your isolation needs today.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): provides per-customer pools and stronger runtime separation; control plane remains Redwood-hosted but we can provide role-based access and long-term audit logs.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): complete control plane residency in your environment (or a private control plane we host inside your VPC). Best fit for strict custody requirements.

Open questions for Clearwell to confirm fit
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrent requests (tokens/min) so we can size Dedicated pools or estimate on-prem hardware.
2) Will Clearwell accept a Dedicated deployment if we provide BYOK for model encryption and an ACL + network egress policy that prevents cross-tenant KV cache access?
3) Any contractual must-haves beyond SOC 2 Type II and standard DPA (e.g., specific log-retention SLAs, forensic availability window)?
4) Timeline constraint for POC and pilot (target go-live month).

Proposed next steps
- Alex to confirm QPS and the three items above (1–3).
- We’ll send a short ops checklist and a POC scope doc as attachments.
- Tech workshop: 45 minutes with Redwood infra + Clearwell infra/security to map control-plane responsibilities. Suggested times: Thu 3/24 or Mon 3/28 (PST).

I’ve attached the POC-scope.pdf and a simple data-flow-diagram.png that maps the Dedicated vs Private deployment differences. If Dedicated meets your gating criteria with BYOK + strict egress rules we can often avoid a full Private control plane.

Thanks,
Ben
--
Ben Carter | Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0109

-----

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwell-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 12:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: segmentation commitment & deployment expectations

Ben / team — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) QPS: steady-state 15 requests/min, peaks about 120 requests/min during batch windows (short bursts up to 300/min). Token sizes variable, averaging ~250 tokens per request.
2) Dedicated path: we are open to Dedicated if the following are guaranteed: 
   - BYOK for encryption at rest and for model keys; we need evidence that keys never leave our KMS account.
   - No Redwood staff or cross-tenant services can use the tenant's runtime tokens without explicit audit tickets.
   - KV cache isolation: must be namespace-isolated per-tenant.
3) Contract must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, DPA, plus a written commitment on log retention (90 days), and proof-of-incident response SLA (48-hour initial response + a 2-week forensics package).
4) Timeline: aiming for a pilot in Q2 (target May start).

Attaching a short security-reqs.xlsx that maps our internal bar.

If Dedicated can satisfy the BYOK + KV isolation + the log-retention commitment, we prefer that route over a full Private control plane (because we want faster time-to-prod). Otherwise we will need a Private deployment.

—Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Infrastructure | Clearwell Analytics
alex.johnson@clearwell-analytics.com | (202) 555-0183

-----

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@clearwell-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22 15:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call: segmentation commitment & deployment expectations

Alex — thanks for the details and the attachment. Short answers and what we can commit to today: 

- BYOK: Supported. For Dedicated deployments we can integrate with your KMS for model artifact encryption and for workspace-level secrets. For the highest assurance we recommend a Private control plane where the KMS is entirely resident in your account; however, Dedicated + BYOK still keeps keys in your KMS and we only store encrypted references. We will document key management flow on the tech workshop.

- KV cache & runtime tokens: Dedicated runtime pools are tenant-specific (no shared GPU process) and we provide namespace isolation for KV caches. Control-plane operations that require higher privileges are logged; we can build a playbook to reduce human access and require ticket-based escalation for sensitive actions.

- Logs & incident response: We can offer 90-day log retention on request for Dedicated (longer-retention is an add-on). Incident response SLA (48-hour initial acknowledgment) is feasible for Enterprise tier; forensic deliverables can be scoped into the SOW.

Next operational steps I propose: 
1) Technical workshop (45m) — Redwood infra + Clearwell infra/security: we’ll map exactly which services interact with KMS and where keys are used.
2) Ops checklist: fill out the attached Redwood Dedicated ops checklist and mark items you require as "must-have" vs "nice-to-have."
3) POC scope agreement: if Dedicated passes gates we’ll spin up a small dedicated pool and run a 2-week POC (we’ll provide test scripts and monitoring dashboards).

Suggested times for the tech workshop: Thu 3/24 10:00–11:00 PDT or Mon 3/28 08:00–08:45 PDT. Please confirm availability.

If you’d like, we can also surface a draft MA that includes the specific log-retention and incident response commitments so legal can speed a redline.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen | Solutions Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0114

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-ops-checklist.pdf
Link: https://docs.redwood.com/ops/checklist/dedicated-vs-private

Subject: Re: Post-call: segmentation commitment & deployment expectations

Looping in a quick note — happy to approve a standard Enterprise term addendum to cover 90-day log retention + 48-hour incident acknowledgement for the CW pilot, subject to legal sign-off. If Alex confirms the Dedicated approach and timeline (pilot May), approve proceeding with the POC and the BYOK integration work.

Marissa
